scenario.kalpNote: KALP (Left To Live On) is a standardized credit assessment used by Swedish banks. It calculates the household's remaining budget after all housing costs and basic living expenses are paid. Living cost definitions are based on figures from Konsumentverket (The Swedish Consumer Agency). The calculation subtracts standard living costs, stressed net interest (higher of scenario rate or 6.5%, after tax deduction), amortization, monthly fees, and operating costs from your estimated net income (accounting for Swedish tax brackets and the jobbskatteavdrag).
scenario.kalpApproved: Banks should likely approve the loan as you have sufficient remaining funds after all housing costs and living expenses.
scenario.kalpMarginal: Banks may reject the final loan despite preliminary approval, as your remaining funds after expenses are limited.
scenario.kalpRejected: Banks will likely reject the loan as you would have negative funds remaining after housing costs and living expenses.
scenario.vtlTooltip: The Loan-to-Value (LTV) requirement: If you borrow more than 50% of the home's value, you must amortize 1% per year. If you borrow more than 70%, you must amortize 2% per year.
scenario.dtiTooltip: The Debt-to-Income (DTI) requirement: If your total household loan exceeds 4.5 times your annual gross income, you must amortize an additional 1% per year.
scenario.dtiRemoved2026: This requirement is removed in the new rules starting April 1st, 2026.
scenario.propertyTaxTooltip: Property tax (Fastighetsavgift) for houses is 0.75% of the tax assessment value, capped at a maximum annual amount. New houses are exempt for the first 15 years.
scenario.greenDiscount: Energy class A or B often qualifies for a 'green mortgage' discount (usually 0.10-0.20%) on your interest rate.

kunskap.title: Bovett Knowledge Base
kunskap.subtitle: Understand Swedish bank requirements and mortgage rules
kunskap.faq1_q: New mortgage rules in 2026 - What do the new rules starting April 1st mean?
kunskap.faq1_a: The new mortgage rules will come into effect on April 1st, 2026. They include raising the mortgage cap to 90% (from 85%) and removing the income-based amortization requirement (the rule stating you must amortize an extra 1% if your loan exceeds 4.5 times your gross income). With Bovett, you can easily simulate how these new rules affect your monthly costs.
kunskap.faq2_q: Why was my loan rejected despite having a loan promise (Lånelöfte)?
kunskap.faq2_a: A loan promise is preliminary and often based on standardized estimates. Once you win a bidding war, the bank calculates a specific KALP (Left to Live On) budget for that exact property. If the property's fees and operating costs, combined with your household budget, cannot survive the bank's high stress-tested interest rate, they may reject the loan. Using Bovett to do your own detailed calculation beforehand helps you avoid these unpleasant surprises.
kunskap.faq3_q: What is KALP (Kvar Att Leva På)?
kunskap.faq3_a: KALP is a standardized calculation model banks use to determine if you can afford the loan. They subtract housing costs, a stress-tested interest rate (often around 6.5 - 7%), amortization, and standardized living expenses from your net after-tax income. A loan is only granted if you have a positive balance in this calculation.
kunskap.faq4_q: Can the bank still deny my loan even if my KALP looks good?
kunskap.faq4_a: Yes, absolutely. The bank always performs a separate valuation of the property itself. If they believe you are overpaying relative to market value, or if the housing association (BRF) has very poor finances, they can refuse to lend for that specific purchase even if your personal finances are perfect.
kunskap.cta_kalp_desc: Want to see exactly how the bank views your finances? Try our interactive KALP Calculator.

kalpCalc.title: KALP Calculator
kalpCalc.description: See if your finances align with the bank's requirements. KALP (Kvar Att Leva På) is the standard test Swedish banks use to determine your mortgage approval.
kalpCalc.stressInterestTooltip: Banks test if you can handle an interest rate of at least 6.5%. This is the cost after the 30% tax deduction.
kalpCalc.livingStandardTooltip: Konsumentverket's standard baseline for food, clothes, transport, etc.
kalpCalc.rejectedDesc: The bank's calculation puts you in the red. You either need a larger downpayment, a cheaper home, or a higher income.
kalpCalc.marginalDesc: You have a positive balance, but the margin is small. Some banks might approve this, but others might require a slightly larger buffer.
kalpCalc.approvedDesc: You have a healthy margin left over after all costs are paid. The bank should feel comfortable approving this loan.
kalpCalc.kalpDetail: KALP stands for 'Kvar Att Leva På' (Left To Live On). It is a standardized calculation Swedish banks use to see how much money your household has left each month after all housing and basic living expenses are paid. Banks often use standardized figures from the Swedish Consumer Agency (Konsumentverket) for basic living costs like food, clothes, and insurance. Additionally, they calculate your interest based on a much higher rate than you actually pay (a 'stress rate') to ensure you can handle future interest rate hikes.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: At Bovett, we take your privacy seriously. This policy describes how we handle your personal information.
privacy.section1_desc: All your property data, income information, and calculation scenarios are stored locally in your browser's LocalStorage. We do not transmit this data to our servers, nor do we have any way to access it.
privacy.section2_desc: Bovett is a calculation tool, not a financial institution. We never perform credit checks (UC/Creditsafe) or report your information to any third parties.
privacy.section3_desc: We use Plausible, a privacy-first analytics tool, to understand how our app is used. No cookies are used, no personal data is stored, and all data processing is performed within the EU. In our mobile applications, we only collect non-linked diagnostic data to improve app performance.
privacy.section4_desc: You can completely reset your data at any time through the settings menu, which will permanently delete all information stored in your browser.
privacy.contact: If you have any questions regarding privacy, please contact us at info@bovett.se

financePlanner.title: Finance & Timeline
financePlanner.subtitle: Plan your move and see when the funds need to be available.
financePlanner.seoDescription: Plan your home purchase step-by-step. Calculate capital gains tax, downpayments, and see when to pay deposits and final settlements. Check if you need a bridge loan.
financePlanner.faq1_a: The downpayment (handpenning), usually 10% of the purchase price, is typically paid when the purchase contract is signed, often about a week after winning the bidding process.
financePlanner.faq2_a: A bridge loan is a temporary loan you take if you move into your new home before you've received the funds from selling your old property. It's used to cover the downpayment during that interim period.
financePlanner.cleaningNote: Pro tip: Book move-out cleaning in advance to avoid stress and unexpected surprises!
financePlanner.tip1_q: How much does move-out cleaning cost?
financePlanner.tip1_a: The cost varies by home size, but expect approx. 2,500 – 5,000 SEK after tax deduction (RUT) for an average apartment.
financePlanner.tip2_q: When should I get home insurance for the new place?
financePlanner.tip2_a: You should ensure your home insurance is active from the move-in day. Contact your provider well in advance to transfer or sign up.
financePlanner.bankWarning: Important: Always contact your bank before signing the purchase contract to get final approval for this specific property.
financePlanner.feesNote: Stamp duty and mortgage deeds are usually paid on the move-in day as part of the final settlement.
financePlanner.bridgeLoanDesc: Since you are moving in before you move out, you will need a temporary loan to cover the downpayment.
financePlanner.estimateNote: The calculation is an estimate and includes capital gains tax (22%).
